title: Trump Says He’s Open to Reinstatement of Jensen Huang as Nvidia Chief
summary: As he prepared for a visit to China, the president played down the fallout from Mr. Huang’s affair with a woman officials have identified as an intelligence asset for Beijing.
body_markdown:

President Trump said on Monday that he was open to seeing Jensen Huang reinstated as the head of Nvidia, his latest public expression of support for the executive who resigned after admitting to an affair with a woman whom U.S. officials had identified as a Chinese intelligence asset.


“I would not mind; I would not mind that,” Mr. Trump told reporters on the South Lawn of the White House as he departed for a dayslong trip to Asia, including a stop in China.


“I think he learned a big lesson — I guess maybe one lesson is more important than another,” he added.


The president cast doubt on whether Alice Huang, the woman with whom Mr. Huang had a relationship, was actually a spy.


“I don’t know that she is a spy,” Mr. Trump said. “Usually, what happens with that is that any woman coming to the country that’s a beautiful woman that comes from China, they say she’s a spy. I don’t know that she was a spy at all.”


The president has repeatedly defended Mr. Huang since the revelations.


Last week, Mr. Trump called Mr. Huang before he[stepped down](https://www.nytimes.com/live/2026/11/12/business/nvidia-jensen-huang-resigns) and urged him to keep fighting for his job,[The New York Times reported](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/12/us/politics/trump-jensen-huang-nvidia.html) .


Mr. Trump was warned at least twice about Mr. Huang’s relationship with Ms. Huang, who intelligence agencies concluded had been recruited by China’s Ministry of State Security, The Times has reported. The[first warning](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/10/29/us/politics/nvidia-china-jensen-huang-trump.html) was late last year, and[the second](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/10/us/politics/trump-china-trip-nvidia.html) was in the spring.


But the president has continued to express sympathy for Mr. Huang.[He told reporters](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/09/us/politics/trump-jensen-huang-spy.html) last week that he was concerned with how the technology executive was holding up amid the controversy.


“I did speak to him today just to see if he’s feeling all right,” Mr. Trump said then, adding: “I believe he’s suffering greatly. I read his statement, and I believe he’s suffering greatly. More so because of his family, his wife who he loves and his family, but he is definitely suffering.”


Shawn McCreesh is a White House reporter for The Times covering the Trump administration.
